# Introducing Basedash Subscriptions

Max Musing Max Musing avatarMax MusingFounder and CEO of Basedash  · August 8, 2026

Today we’re launching Basedash Subscriptions — subscribe to any dashboard or chart, and Basedash delivers a fresh snapshot to your inbox or a Slack channel on the schedule you pick.

Set it once: every Monday at 9:00 AM, to #metrics and your inbox. From then on, the report just shows up — up-to-date charts, with a link back to the live dashboard for anyone who wants to dig in.

## Why we built it [...] Subscriptions are available today for all Basedash users:

1. Sign up for Basedash (or log in) and open any dashboard or chart
2. Open the menu and choose Subscribe
3. Pick your schedule and destinations, and create the subscription
4. Go do something else — the report will find you

## What’s next

The best report is the one nobody had to remember to send.

Subscribe to your data — delivered on schedule.

Written by

Max Musing avatar

## Max Musing

Founder and CEO of Basedash [...] ## Subscribe to any dashboard or chart

Open the menu on any dashboard or chart and hit Subscribe. Pick your schedule with a simple structured sentence — every day, weekdays, a weekly day, monthly or quarterly on a date, at whatever hour you want. It reads exactly like you’d say it: every week on Monday at 9:00 AM.

Then choose where it goes under Deliver to: email it to yourself or any set of teammates, send it to a Slack channel, or both. Click Create subscription and you’re done — there is no step three.

## Delivered where your team already looks

When the schedule fires, Basedash renders a fresh snapshot of every chart and sends it out:

1. Open the dashboard and click the ”…” menu in the header (or right-click the dashboard in the sidebar)
2. Select “Subscribe”
3. Set a schedule — daily, weekdays, weekly, monthly, or quarterly — and a delivery time
4. Add at least one destination: email recipients, a Slack channel, or both
5. Click “Create subscription”

Every chart on the dashboard is included as an image in the delivered snapshot. You can create multiple subscriptions per dashboard, and pause or delete them anytime from the same menu.

Subscriptions send a snapshot of the dashboard as it looks right now. For AI-generated analysis and custom write-ups on a schedule, see automations.

## ​ Sharing and collaboration [...] ### ​ AI iteration

You can ask Basedash to add charts, update existing charts, change the layout, or refine the dashboard after it has been created. This is useful when you want to start from a broad dashboard prompt and then narrow the result into the exact operating view your team needs.

### ​ Filters

 Add dashboard-wide filters
 Create date range selectors
 Filter by specific dimensions
 Apply filters to multiple charts

### ​ Auto-refresh

By default, dashboards refresh every 15 minutes to keep your data up-to-date. You can change the refresh interval to fit your needs.

# Scheduled reports in BI tools: how automated report delivery works

Max Musing Max Musing avatarMax MusingFounder and CEO of Basedash  · June 20, 2026

A scheduled report is a saved report or dashboard that a BI tool runs on a recurring schedule and delivers to people automatically, usually by email or Slack, without anyone opening the tool. The point is reach: most people who need a number will never log into a dashboard, but they will read an email at 8am or glance at a Slack message. Scheduling turns a dashboard that a few analysts visit into a report that a whole team receives. [...] A scheduled report runs on a cron-style schedule, renders to a format (PDF, image, CSV, or link), and pushes to a channel (email, Slack, webhook, or file storage).
 Scheduled reports, alerts, and live dashboards solve different problems. Use a schedule for routine reach, an alert for exceptions, and a live dashboard for investigation.
 The most common failures are timing races (the report fires before the data refreshes), time zone mistakes, and silent empty reports after a query breaks.
 Report bursting sends one report definition to many recipients with each person seeing only their own slice. It depends on row-level filtering, not separate reports.
 Treat every scheduled report like a small data pipeline: it needs an owner, a freshness guarantee, a failure path, and an expiry date.
